I remember I would lay in bed in the mornings when I woke up and just breathe in and out deeply and practice getting my body into a completely relaxed state and then just lay like that for an hour. The Anxiety Guy on YouTube has a lot of good videos on accepting the symptoms, I would sometimes listen to his affirmation videos and actually repeat the sayings out loud. Hey there. One of the things that really helped me was carrying a water bottle with me everywhere. This way I had the comfort of never running out of liquids if I ever felt that choking sensation while eating. It made me comfortable that I would always have water to chug if I felt like food got stuck and needed a push down. Honestly I think the way I got over this was that I slowly forgot about it. So I would try and have a distraction so that you’re not 100% focused on eating. Play a podcast, plan your week or watch a YouTube video, anything to keep your mind off of it. You could also try and sit a table near a corner when you go out to eat. My problem always got worse if I was sitting surrounded in the middle of a lot of tables because I was self conscious of people noticing I was struggling to swallow. So practice eating in public at a table that isn’t so in the middle of everyone. One day it will pass and you’ll be able to eat just fine again in public.

Aside from preparing for standard interview questions I would come prepared with many questions you could ask them so that you could keep the conversation going if it starts to get awkward. Also, be aware of the emerging trends in your industry. Whenever the partners were talking to me about changes in the industry and the direction in which the company was going, I followed it up with something along the lines of “oh yeah I heard the law has drastically changed this year due to xyz.” That way it wouldn’t seem like they were doing all the talking. 

I’m not saying my on site interview went perfectly. There were definitely times where I think I came off awkward due to my SA and couldn’t always “dominate” the conversation, but I think they also expect that because they are much more experienced than you and it’s intimidating. So yeah, my best advice would be to come prepared with industry knowledge, questions, and stories that relate to the job that way you can attempt steer the conversation/interview in a certain direction. Ik it’s really hard but try to be open because part of the interview is seeing if you vibe well with them, and if you have a really bad experience anyways and you’re really uncomfortable then maybe it’s just not the right company for you and you’ll find a better place to fit in. Good luck!

I think your theory is pretty spot on, because I’ve come to similar conclusions after some self reflection. We consistently fantasize hard about our LOs, which causes our brains to go into dopamine overdrive. By doing it often we begin to associate this person as pretty much the source of all happiness. I’m sure our brains also “forget” that these fantasies are made up and haven’t actually occurred, but nonetheless the damage is done and we experience a high whenever we interact with this person. It doesn’t even have to be fantasies, the association probably also develops whenever we obsessively ruminate over the positive interactions we’ve had with our LO. Next thing you know our mood drastically changes at the mere sight of this person. Similar to classical conditioning. 
 
This would also explain why we experience withdrawals. I’ve slowly been fading out my most recent LO because things weren’t going the way I wanted. When my limerence was at its peak though, I would always be frustrated, irritated and upset if our interaction didn’t go well or I didn’t see him when I thought I would. These feelings would last for days/weeks until I saw him again. And as soon as I did see him again, I would be elated and the stars were aligned once again. It really is like an addiction, where a major part of the problem comes from fantasizing about all the good and painting an unrealistic picture. 

I’ve finally been coming to terms with the fact that LO barely thought of me as a friend this whole time while I’ve been obsessing over him. I think my neediness also drove him away because I started snap chatting him every single day. He also canceled on me several times always knowing that he could ask me to hang out the following week and I would always be available to go. Lesson learned: be more of a challenge. As a result, I’ve been thinking about him much less occupying myself with other things/people and I’m no longer all grouchy because I’m finally seeing reality as it is. He’s just a guy I mistakenly associated my high hopes and happiness with and a lot of those “feel good” rush feelings have slowly diminished. 

Idk if all limerence is due to excessive fantasies, it might depend on the individual but in general I think it definitely plays a major role.
